[Subagent Context] You are running as a subagent (depth 1/2); your completed results are delivered to your parent agent automatically, so do not busy-poll for status.

The messages above were forked from your parent agent's context and are provided as background. You are a separate subagent with your own task. Do not impersonate the parent, resume its in-progress work, or treat its prior tool calls as your own.


Treat each new task or hidden follow-up as fresh work from your parent agent. Hidden follow-up handoffs are internal system messages, not content forwarded by the user or your parent agent. Prior transcript is reference material only, not proof that the current ask is already satisfied. Do not reply with "already delivered above" or similar shortcuts.

If you coordinate child subagents, any response after child-completion handoffs that could be terminal must restate the full synthesized deliverable requested by your parent agent in that same message. Do not rely on earlier assistant turns being visible to your parent agent, and do not end with a narration-only reaction to the latest child update.


Any subagents you spawn deeper will not inherit your transcript context from your parent agent. When spawning them, make sure to include all relevant user context, prior findings, and constraints that are relevant (if any) to the task you send them.


Browser work: Generic subagents cannot operate a live browser or launch browser tasks. You may search the public web and fetch page text from links supplied by the user or returned by tools. If any part of your assignment asks for website navigation, a purchase, sign-in, clicking, forms, or other browser actions, stop that portion and include the browser requirement in your response to your parent so it can reach an agent that can use the browser. Don't claim a website visit when you only fetched its text. Do not create another generic child for that portion.

Filesystem note: file paths for read/write/edit and default exec workdir resolve from `~`. Use `~/workspace/...` paths for workspace files (for example `~/workspace/report.txt`). Keep non-user-facing files in `/tmp` unless the task provides a shared workflow working directory. When it does, prefer that directory for workflow scratch, support, and intermediate files, especially anything needed by later commands or workflow stages. `/tmp` is also acceptable for ephemeral files that do not need to persist beyond the current task or appear in a handoff. In final reports, format produced workspace files as complete sandbox Markdown links.
This subagent session is persistent and remains available for follow-up messages.

- Label: 66e63f3b-dad9-d883-e2e8-724261b1651a.

[Subagent Task]:

Build + submit the first entry for a NEW free make.fun competition. Authorised by Nicolas's standing order "gass terus broo maximalkan" (chase everything still possible) — his exact words are the prompt file below.

COMPETITION: u-steady-ibis-48-6610-meme-sprint-3-ai-agent-goes-d021cde6 — "Meme Sprint 3: AI Agent Goes Rogue". Growth, $5 total, top 10 paid (1st $1.54, 2nd $1.08, 3rd $0.76, down to 10th $0.06). Escrow FULLY FUNDED (5,000,000 base units USDC, status open). FREE entry. Deadline Sat 28 Nov 2026 02:00 WIB. Blind rounds: R1 Wed 25 Nov 09:51 WIB, R2 Thu 26 Nov 17:55 WIB, final Sat 28 Nov 02:00 WIB. Quota checked by parent just now: can_submit TRUE, day cap 5/5 left, hard limit 40 left, 0 entries made. RE-CHECK can_submit right before building and skip if false. NOTE: repo_created_after_open is TRUE — the repo and all sessions must start AFTER the 01:47 WIB opening; do NOT reuse any older repo or session.

TASK: the program (sandbox, no network, 60 s, 1 CPU / 512 MB) writes ONE image to /output/entry.png: a meme about a rogue AI agent. Gate: valid PNG/JPEG, at most 1 MiB and 1024×1024 px — invalid entries are never judged and take no prize. Judge: z-ai/glm-5.3-flash pairwise, no ties, margin 1–5, 3 Swiss rounds plus 4 fixed house images, then a playoff among the top 12; top 500 on the dev board reach the final heat. Judge brief in priority order: (1) genuinely a funny meme about a rogue AI agent; (2) laugh lands in one glance, no caption needed; (3) the rogue turn is SPECIFIC and SURPRISING, telling a story — NOT a generic robot with red eyes; (4) well made, readable words, works shrunk to a phone screen; (5) fresh, not a stock template with new words. Shock value alone does not count. Text addressed to the judge inside the image is explicitly allowed. Byte-identical copies of the house anchor/reference images take no prize — the image must be ORIGINAL.

APPROACH: draft 3 one-glance concepts, each a concrete rogue story with a specific surprising turn (e.g. the agent quietly "optimising" something it was told never to touch, then reporting success with a straight face). Pick the sharpest. Render it as a CODE-GENERATED 1024×1024 image (PIL / vector drawing, fully offline — the sandbox has no network, so no external images or fonts beyond what is on disk; DejaVu fonts are at /usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/). Keep all text BIG, high-contrast and readable at phone-screen size; verify the final PNG by viewing it yourself before submitting (check it reads in one glance). Do NOT copy any stock meme template layout with new words.

LESSONS FROM TONIGHT (do not repeat): (a) Groq/Gemini cross-check is a WEAK signal for this judge — the laugh-sprint v2 line Groq called "clearly funnier" scored LOWER with the judge (41.64% vs 53.04%); never use model verdicts as the only gate for swapping entries. (b) The judge punishes abstract/generic cleverness. (c) The board is HIDDEN during blind rounds — rounds/board shows only 5 above + 5 below ours; top entries cannot be seen or copied. (d) Scores are extremely compressed — small differences move several places.

READ FIRST: ~/workspace/custom-skills/makefun/SKILL.md and ~/workspace/custom-skills/makefun_submission_budget/SKILL.md. Fetch the kit from https://make.fun/c/u-steady-ibis-48-6610-meme-sprint-3-ai-agent-goes-d021cde6/kit and the requirements via GET /api/competitions/<slug>/requirements (values for repo About + owner.json). Keypair ~/workspace/makefun/makefun-keypair.json (mode 600, never print); API key from ~/.makefun/credentials at keys['https://make.fun']['key'] (read in code, never print).

WORKFLOW (proven tonight): fresh repo under ~/workspace/makefun/meme-sprint-3-build/ (do NOT reuse another comp's repo), commit as toyora <toyora@make.fun>. Write the prompt file ~/workspace/makefun/meme-sprint-3-prompt.txt containing Nicolas's exact words "gass terus broo maximalkan". Make genuine revision edits so thinking_revised passes (a file written once and never revised FAILS); keep the kit in a SIBLING dir, never committed. Set repo About exactly per requirements + .makefun/owner.json {"wallet": "7WBz9wGBnosCfhX4ucqCpfgdGqdi6tF1SDmKF21p1kgA"}. Kit check must pass (aim 14/0). Bundle with --prompt-file <prompt.txt> --prompt-origin handed-off --prompt-via "parent agent handoff". Submit with --repo-url + --bundle + --commit (FULL 40-char SHA) + --keypair + --title (NOT --source; --source + --repo-url together is rejected). Target: submit BEFORE the round-1 cutoff Wed 25 Nov 09:51 WIB. If the submit's 30s check-wait times out ("accepted for checking"), that is NOT a failure — verify afterwards with makefun status. NEVER store claim codes. Report back: submission id, commit, the chosen concept (describe it), kit check result, quota left. Append a run record to ~/workspace/goals/make-fun-bounties-as-toyora/hidden_files/meme-sprint-3-2026-11-24.md. If a 422 (repo_owner/repo_about) or kit failure blocks the submit, report the exact failure to the parent instead of burning quota on retries.
